Pronunciation: The Final 'S'

In French the final s is silent. In English it is not.

One rule, three grammars

the pronunciation rule is the same for the plural, the genitive and the third person singular.

two circuits  ·  the engineer's report  ·  it works

There are three possible pronunciations. The sound in front decides

/z//s//ɪz/
after a voiced consonant, and after any vowel

cables · sensors · wires
it runs · it controls		 after a voiceless consonant

circuits · outputs · chips
it works · it starts		 after a sibilant
(and it adds a whole syllable)

switches · fuses · devices
it charges

One rule and one exception:

/z/ is the normal ending.
It becomes /s/ only when the sound before it is voiceless, because you cannot switch your voice on that fast.

Fingers on the throat. Say the end of cab, then the end of cup. /b/ buzzes and /p/ does not.

1 · The four noises

Everything on this page depends on recognising one family of sounds. Do these out loud.

Zzzzzz
/z/
be the bee
Ssssss
/s/
be the snake
Shhhhh
/ʃ/
ask for silence
Jjjjjj
/ʒ/
say "joujou"

Those are sibilants: consonants that hiss or buzz, made by sending air at your teeth. Add the two that are the same noises with a stop on the front, and the full list is six.

/s/   /z/   /ʃ/   /tʃ/   /ʒ/   /dʒ/
pass  ·  size  ·  wish  ·  watch  ·  garage  ·  bridge

Now find them.

Click every word that ends in one of those six sounds. Say each one aloud first.

3 · Why an extra syllable?

/ɪz/ exists to make the /s/ or /z/ audible.

Try it. Say fuse, then try to add an s straight on the end without changing anything. You cannot. An s after an s is an s. So English pushes a small vowel in front of it, and the word grows a syllable.

one syllabletwo syllables
switchswitches  SWITCH-iz
fusefuses  FEW-ziz
bridgebridges  BRIDG-iz
circuitno. circuits stays one syllable, with a clean s on the end

4 · The same rule, wearing an apostrophe

Tap any of them to hear it.

genitivesoundbecause
Mike's cat/s/Mike ends in /k/, voiceless
Rose's cat/ɪz/Rose already ends in a buzz. ROH-ziz
Tess's car/ɪz/TESS-iz. The one everybody gets wrong
the engineer's report/z/ends in a vowel sound, and vowels are voiced
my parents' meeting/s/ends in /t/, voiceless. The apostrophe is silent
the girls' car/z/ends in /l/, voiced

Notice the last two. My parents' meeting and the girls' car have no extra s written at all, and they are still pronounced with the ending they already had. The apostrophe never makes a sound. It only tells you who owns the thing.

5 · Say it

The orange endings are the ones that add a syllable. Every other s is there and must be heard.

The board has four outputs, two inputs and six test points. (three /s/, no extra syllables)
The sensors and the cables go to the motors. (three /z/, the normal ending)
Check the switches, the fuses and the bridges. (three extra syllables, and you can hear all three)
It works, it runs, it charges and it measures the current.
The engineer's report says the devices failed.
/s/circuits · outputs · volts · chips · watts · sockets · it works · it starts · it detects
/z/cables · sensors · wires · motors · coils · valves · signals · it runs · it controls · it measures
/ɪz/switches · fuses · bridges · devices · boxes · phases · gauges · interfaces · it charges · it produces
